data.one_liner: Use Drift with a sqlite_async database in the same application.
data.what_it_does: Allows using Drift and sqlite_async together on the same database. Synchronizes table updates between both APIs and supports transactions, migrations, and concurrent reads.
use_when: You want to use Drift ORM features alongside sqlite_async database capabilities.
You need concurrent read queries while writes are happening in SQLite.
avoid_when: You do not need sqlite_async and can use standard Drift database connections directly.
Your project relies on read-only transactions in Drift, which are not currently supported.
strengths: Seamless integration between Drift and sqlite_async APIs.
Automatic propagation of table updates and watching queries across both systems.
Supports transactions, nested transactions, and Drift migrations.
weaknesses: Read-only transactions are not currently supported in Drift.
Web support requires manual placement of sqlite3 WASM and web worker files.
data.setup_notes: Requires setting up SqliteAsyncDriftConnection and configuring web worker/WASM assets if targeting the web platform.

alternatives.name: drift
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want to use Drift directly without sqlite_async integration.

alternatives.name: sqflite
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer the standard SQLite plugin for Flutter without advanced async connection pooling.
